codeReview.summary: The feature adds a prose/footnote retrieval channel and wires it into retrieve(), but it introduces a blocking contract regression: retrieve() can return more than top_k results because supplementary prose/footnote entries are appended after the top_k table loop without a global cap.

issues.description: retrieve() violates its top_k contract by appending up to 3 prose/footnote entries after already collecting top_k table entries (see top_k break at lines 1324-1325). Repro from current code: retrieve_from_question(<UID0001 question>, top_k=1) returns 4 entries (1 fts + 3 prose_footnote). This changes caller-facing behavior and can unexpectedly inflate downstream context size/latency.

New integration assertions are weak and can pass even when no prose/footnote entries are present. For example, channels assertion accepts any of {fts, metric, prose_footnote}, and content-field test iterates over pf_entries without asserting that pf_entries is non-empty.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared architecture/state docs still describe retrieve_v2 as a two-channel retriever, which is now stale after this feature added prose/footnote retrieval.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/architecture.md:17 says "Two-channel funnel: FTS (broad) + metric substring"; mission AGENTS.md:44 says "two-channel retrieval (FTS + metric substring)".

summary: Reviewed handoff, commit diff, transcript skeleton, and skill/procedural context. Implementation generally matches feature intent, but a blocking top_k contract regression in retrieve() means this feature should not pass scrutiny in its current form.
